chunk-001:c002.proposition: Naturalism accommodates suffering as part of nature, whereas divine omnipotence and perfect love imply that every apparently evil event must contribute to a greater good.

orphanFallback.rationale: The same comparison stands constructively as an independent tension: naturalism expects suffering, while the specified divine attributes appear to require a greater-good account of it.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Evolutionary selection explains widespread aversion to suffering and the social impulse to improve conditions through dispositions favoring survival, reproduction, longevity, and prosperity.

orphanFallback.rationale: Presented independently, the evolutionary account positively explains harm avoidance and social concern through inherited dispositions without presupposing a prior challenge about transcendent morality.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Cooperation can be evolutionarily advantageous, while changing Christian treatment of women and slavery weakens the claim that Christianity uniquely supplies unchanging objective moral guidance.

orphanFallback.rationale: The move can constructively combine an evolutionary basis for cooperation with historical changes in Christian moral practice as evidence against a unique, unchanging guidance claim.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: Because an omnipotent and perfectly loving God knowingly permits each evil, Christianity must hold that even apparently gratuitous suffering and atrocities contribute to a superior outcome.

orphanFallback.rationale: As a standalone argument, the stated divine attributes generate the greater-good requirement directly, allowing its application to apparently gratuitous suffering without an earlier opposing move.

chunk-002:c002-02.proposition: Christian promises of future healing merit skepticism, and restricting their benefit to believers would treat sincere unbelievers incompatibly with the perfect love attributed to God.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition independently challenges both the warrant and moral adequacy of future-restoration promises by examining their plausibility and their alleged exclusion of sincere unbelievers.

chunk-002:c002-05.proposition: Natural uncertainty can explain selective surprising recoveries, whereas genuine divine healing should also produce clear outcomes such as restored limbs rather than only ambiguous remissions.

orphanFallback.rationale: The contrast supplies a self-contained evidential test: compare recoveries expected under biological uncertainty with the unmistakable interventions expected from omnipotent divine healing.

chunk-002:c002-06.proposition: Sincere unbelievers cannot force conviction in weak religious claims, so eternally punishing earnest nonbelief is inconsistent with an all-loving God who controls the salvific system.

orphanFallback.rationale: The distinction between unwilling rejection and inability to become convinced independently establishes a moral challenge to belief-conditioned salvation under an all-loving God.

chunk-002:c002-09.proposition: A system that may save a sincerely converted genocidal offender while condemning a decent but unconvinced atheist reverses proportionate moral outcomes and conflicts with a good God.

orphanFallback.rationale: The comparison functions independently as a test of proportional justice, contrasting belief-conditioned outcomes for a grave offender and a morally decent sincere unbeliever.
